title: What c does to a line

files.lesson.md: --- order: 7 unit: lines node: AC9M8A04 n2 uses: [AC9M7N07 n2] # negative c and outputs title: What c does to a line summary: In y = mx + c, the number on its own moves the line up or down without changing its steepness, so lines with the same m are parallel. language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "Two phone plans charge the same price per gigabyte but different monthly fees. What do their graphs look like?" connection: plans-cross # data/connections/maths.yml app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8136 url: http://127.0.0.1:8136/index.html readySelector: "#sl-c" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: graph.yml#explain-pic, caption: "$y = 2x + 4$ is $y = 2x + 1$ moved up 3. Same $m$, so they are parallel." } explainClip: query: { code: "@graph.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "c moves the line up or down; the steepness stays the same" say: "c moves the line up or down, and the steepness stays the same." clip: - caption: { text: "The dashed line is y = 2x + 1. The solid line starts the same.", say: "The dashed line is y equals two x plus one; the solid starts the same." } - wait: 400 - caption: { text: "A bigger c moves the line up. It stays just as steep.", say: "A bigger c moves the line up, and it stays just as steep." } - click: Make c bigger - wait: 400 - caption: { text: "c = 4: the line crosses the y-axis at 4.", say: "With c equal to four, the line crosses the y axis at four." } - caption: { text: "Same m, so it is parallel to the dashed line.", say: "It has the same m, so it is parallel to the dashed line." } - wait: 400 - caption: { text: "A negative c moves it below: c = −2 crosses at −2.", say: "A negative c moves it down: c of negative two crosses at negative two." } - click: Make c smaller - click: Make c smaller - expect: { selector: "#legend", contains: "y = 2x − 2" } - wait: 1200 --- With $c$ kept at 1, you changed $m$, the steepness. Now $m$ stays at 2 and you change $c$, the number on its own. ## Predict: a bigger c ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to what c will do before moving it shows whether students have separated c from m." check: type: predict q: "The line $y = 2x + 1$ has $c = 1$. If $c$ becomes 4, so the rule is $y = 2x + 4$, what happens to the line?" options: - "It moves up by 3, and is just as steep" - "It gets steeper" - "It crosses the $x$-axis at 4" - "It moves 3 to the right" actual: "It moves up by 3 and is just as steep. Every value of y is 3 more than before (2x + 4 instead of 2x + 1), so the whole line moves up 3. m is still 2, so the steepness is the same." ``` $$y = 2x + 1 \quad\longrightarrow\quad y = 2x + 4$$ Work out $y$ when $x = 0$ for each rule. Then think about what happens at $x = 1$. ## Run: change c ```step stage: run insight: "Moving c while m stays fixed slides the line up and down: the step stays 'up 2', and the line never turns." try: { playground: board, starter: "graph.yml#run", height: 680 } check: { type: board, text: "Set $c$ to 4. Was your prediction right?", when: "c = 4" } ``` Change $c$ and compare the solid line with the dashed line, $y = 2x + 1$. Watch the step, and the two rows of the table. ## Investigate: reading c ```step stage: investigate insight: "c is where the line crosses the y-axis (the value of y when x is 0). Lines with the same m are parallel; only c tells them apart." tasks: - picture: { ref: graph.yml#explain-pic, caption: "Each $y$ on $y = 2x + 4$ is 3 more than on $y = 2x + 1$: the line moves up 3." } check: type: answer q: "Where does the line $y = 3x - 5$ cross the $y$-axis? Give the value of $y$." answer: "-5" feedback: - ["3", "3 is m, the steepness. The line crosses the y-axis where x = 0: work out y there."] - ["5", "Check the sign: when x = 0, y = 3 × 0 − 5."] explain: "−5. When x = 0, y = 3 × 0 − 5 = −5, which is c." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#ana" text: "Ana decides whether two lines are parallel. Click the line where her reasoning goes wrong." answer: 4 fault: logic misconception: parallel-same-numbers explain: "Line 4: parallel lines need the same m, the number in front of x. Here m is 2 and 5, so one is steeper than the other: they are not parallel." - check: type: question q: "Which line is parallel to $y = 3x + 1$?" options: ["$y = x + 3$", "$y = 3x - 4$", "$y = -3x + 1$"] answer: 1 explain: "y = 3x − 4 has the same m, 3, so it is just as steep: it is y = 3x + 1 moved down 5." ``` ### Where it crosses Here is how to read $c$ from a rule. ```worked y = 2x + 4 :: Where does this line cross the $y$-axis, and how does it compare with $y = 2x + 1$? x = 0: \; y = 2(0) + 4 = 4 :: The $y$-axis is where $x = 0$. Put 0 in place of $x$. c = 4 :: $2x$ is 0 there, so $y$ is just $c$: the line crosses at 4. x = 1: \; 2(1) + 4 = 6, \; 2(1) + 1 = 3 :: Compare the two rules at $x = 1$. 6 - 3 = 3 :: $y$ is 3 more, and it is 3 more at every $x$, because only $c$ changed. \text{same } m \Rightarrow \text{parallel} :: The line moved up 3 without turning: lines with the same $m$ are parallel. ``` ### Find the mistake Read Ana's working one line at a time. Which line does not follow? ### Parallel Which number has to match? ## Modify: change c on purpose ```step stage: modify insight: "One change at a time: a negative c, c = 0 (through the origin), a point that is not on the y-axis, then both numbers at once for a parallel line." try: { playground: board, starter: "graph.yml#below", height: 600 } tasks: - starter: "graph.yml#below" hint: "T is on the y-axis. Where must the line cross it?" check: { type: board, text: "Set $c$ so the line passes through $T(0, -2)$.", when: "T on y = 2x + c", explain: "c = −2: the line crosses the y-axis at −2." } - starter: "graph.yml#origin" hint: ["Work out 2x at T: 2 × 2 = 4.", "T is at y = 4, so how much is left for c?"] check: { type: board, text: "Set $c$ so the line passes through $T(2, 4)$.", when: "T on y = 2x + c", explain: "c = 0: y = 2x passes through (0, 0), the origin." } - starter: "graph.yml#off-axis" hint: ["At T, x = 1, so 2x is 2.", "y at T is 6. What do you add to 2 to get 6?"] check: { type: board, text: "Set $c$ so the line passes through $T(1, 6)$.", when: "T on y = 2x + c", explain: "c = 4: at x = 1, y = 2 + 4 = 6." } - starter: "graph.yml#parallel" hint: ["Parallel means the same steepness. What is m for the dashed line?", "Then set c so the line crosses the y-axis at T."] check: { type: board, text: "Make a line parallel to the dashed line $y = -x + 3$ that passes through $T(0, -1)$.", when: "m = -1 and T on y = mx + c", explain: "m = −1 (same as the dashed line, so parallel) and c = −1 (it crosses at T)." } ``` ### Below the axis Each task puts a point $T$ on the board. Set $c$ so the line passes through $T(0, -2)$. ### Through the origin Now take the line through $T(2, 4)$. What is $c$? ### Not on the axis $T(1, 6)$ is not on the $y$-axis. Work out $2x$ at $T$ first. ### Parallel Two sliders now. Make a line parallel to the dashed one, through $T(0, -1)$. ## Practise: read the line ```step stage: practise insight: "Reading c, recognising parallel lines and finding c from a point are one skill; the review question keeps m from the last lesson fresh." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "Where does $y = 5x + 7$ cross the $y$-axis? Give the value of $y$." answer: "7" feedback: - ["5", "5 is m, the steepness. Put x = 0 into the rule."] explain: "7: when x = 0, y = 5 × 0 + 7 = 7." - check: type: question q: "Which two lines are parallel?" options: - "$y = 4x + 1$ and $y = 4x - 3$" - "$y = 4x + 1$ and $y = x + 4$" - "$y = 4x + 1$ and $y = 2x + 1$" answer: 0 explain: "Both have m = 4, so they are equally steep. y = 4x + 1 and y = x + 4 use the same numbers but in different places; y = 4x + 1 and y = 2x + 1 cross at (0, 1)." - check: type: answer q: "The line $y = 2x + c$ passes through $(3, 10)$. What is $c$?" answer: "4" feedback: - ["10", "10 is y at x = 3. Work out 2x there first: 2 × 3 = 6."] - ["7", "Check: 2 × 3 = 6, and 6 + 7 = 13, not 10."] explain: "At x = 3, 2x = 6. 6 + c = 10, so c = 4." - check: type: answer q: "Review: how far does $y = -3x + 2$ go up for each step right? (A negative answer means it goes down.)" answer: "-3" feedback: - ["2", "2 is c, where the line crosses the y-axis. Look at the number in front of x."] - ["3", "Check the sign: −3 means the line goes down 3 for each step right."] explain: "m = −3: down 3 for each step right." ``` ### From the rule ### Parallel ### From a point ### Review ## Make: a parallel line ```step stage: make insight: "Choosing a point and then finding the c that reaches it, with m fixed, reverses the lesson: from the picture to the rule." try: { playground: board, starter: "graph.yml#make", height: 600 } hint: ["Drag P first. Then work out 2x at P.", "c is the y of P minus 2x."] check: { type: board, text: "Drag $P$ anywhere, then set $c$ so a line parallel to $y = 2x + 1$ passes through it.", when: "P on y = 2x + c", explain: "Your line has m = 2, like the dashed one, so they are parallel, and P is on it." } ``` Choose where $P$ goes, then find the $c$ that takes the line through it. Check: is your line parallel to the dashed one? Stretch: write the rule of the line parallel to $y = 2x + 1$ that passes through $(5, 0)$. ## Make: where two phone plans meet, on paper ```step stage: make insight: "c is the amount paid once, a fee when positive and a credit when negative; where two plans cost the same is where their rules are equal." hint: ["Write each plan as T = (rate) × g + c. Is the credit a plus or a minus?", "Set the two rules equal, then collect the g terms on one side."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "Plan A costs 7 dollars a month plus 3 dollars per GB. Plan B costs 5 dollars per GB with a 9 dollar credit taken off. On paper, write a rule for each plan, then find how many GB make them cost the same." steps: - ["Plan A: $T = 3g + 7$. Plan B: $T = 5g - 9$", "c is the amount paid once: a fee of +7, a credit of −9"] - ["Same cost: $3g + 7 = 5g - 9$", "the plans cost the same where the two rules give the same T"] - ["$16 = 2g$, so $g = 8$. Check: $3 \\times 8 + 7 = 31$ and $5 \\times 8 - 9 = 31$", "put 8 back into both rules"] picks: - step: 2 q: "How do you find where the two plans cost the same?" options: - "Make the two rules equal: 3g + 7 = 5g − 9" - "Make the two fixed amounts equal: 7 = −9" - "Add the two rules together" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "7 and −9 are only where the lines start. Equal costs need the whole rules to be equal.", "Adding gives the cost of both plans together, not where they match."] answer: "8" tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["31", "31 dollars is the cost where they meet. How many GB is that?"] - ["16", "16 is 7 + 9. Divide by the 2 dollars a GB that separates the rates."] criteria: - "I wrote the credit as a minus: c = −9." - "I made the two rules equal." - "I checked 8 GB in both rules and got the same cost." explain: "3g + 7 = 5g − 9 gives 16 = 2g, so g = 8. At 8 GB both plans cost 31 dollars." ``` Do this one in your book, not on the screen. The plans are made up for the task, and real plans have limits on data. Write both rules, make them equal, solve, and check your answer in both. **Also used in** - **Phone and internet plans.** A fee, a credit and a rate are all just c and m. - **Hire and subscriptions.** A joining fee is a positive c, a sign-up discount a negative c. - **Break-even.** A business finds where cost and income lines cross, the same way. ```teacher summary: Students vary c in y = 2x + c on a graph board, find that c moves the line up or down and is where it crosses the y-axis, and that lines with the same m are parallel (AC9M8A04, node 2). time: 45 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 15 min · Modify 12 min · Practise and Make 10 min goals: - I can describe what happens to the line y = mx + c when c changes. - I can read where a line crosses the y-axis from its rule. - I can tell from their rules whether two lines are parallel. struggle: "Separating c from m. Ask: what is y when x is 0? Which number did that, and which number set the steepness?" before: > Do the Run and Modify boards yourself first. This lesson follows "What m does to a line": students should already read m as "up for each step right". Here m stays at 2 and only c changes, so every line is parallel to the dashed y = 2x + 1. The last Modify task is the first time both sliders appear: it is the stretch point of the lesson. The lesson says "where the line crosses the y-axis". The primer has the formal word, y-intercept, if you want to introduce it at the end. running: - "Predict: take a show of hands. The common wrong answer is 'it gets steeper': students expect any bigger number to steepen the line. Do not correct it yet." - "Run: ask students to compare the step on the solid line with the dashed line as they move c. It stays 'up 2'. Then read across a column of the table: each y is the same amount more." - "Investigate: model the worked example live. Put x = 0 into y = 2x + 4 and say 'on the y-axis, x is 0, so 2x is 0 and y is just c'. Then compare both rules at x = 1." - "Modify: before 'Not on the axis', ask: why can't we just read c off the graph here? (T is not on the y-axis.)" - "Practise: the parallel question plants the same numbers in different places. Ask a student who chose it to work out the steepness of each line." - "Make: collect two students' answers and check them as a class: work out 2x at P and subtract from y." - "Paper: the plans task in Make is worked in books; the page marks the number (8) and the reason for making the rules equal. Books out, then check 8 in both rules." stuck: - see: A student says a bigger c makes the line steeper. ask: How far up is the step on each line? fix: "Point at the two steps: both are 'up 2'. Only the starting height on the y-axis changed." - see: A student reads m as where the line crosses the y-axis. ask: What is y when x is 0? Put 0 in the rule. fix: "Work it through: 3 × 0 − 5 = −5. The x term disappears at x = 0, so only c is left." - see: A student says lines with the same numbers are parallel (Ana's mistake). ask: Which number sets the steepness? fix: "Compare m only: same m means same steepness, so parallel. Different m means the lines cross somewhere." - see: A student cannot find c when T is not on the y-axis. ask: What is 2x at T? How much more is y? fix: "Write y = 2x + c with T's numbers in: 6 = 2 × 1 + c, so c = 4. (This is the first equation-solving step of the next lesson.)" stretch: "Write the rule of the line parallel to y = 2x + 1 through (5, 0). Then: can two different lines with the same m ever cross? Why not?" support: "Keep the Run board open for the Investigate questions: set c to the number in the rule and read where the line crosses the y-axis. Use squared paper to draw the two parallel lines." leads: > Next: solving equations with graphs. 2x + 3 = 11 becomes the point where y = 2x + 3 meets y = 11, which joins this unit to the Equations unit. Then modelling: two plans with different m and c, and where their lines cross. Where it leads in class: a fixed starting amount plus a rate (a call-out fee and an hourly charge, a deposit and weekly savings). c is the starting amount; m is the rate. exit: q: Are y = 3x + 2 and y = 3x − 5 parallel? Where does each cross the y-axis? a: Yes, both have m = 3. The first crosses at 2, the second at −5. explain: > In $y = mx + c$, $c$ is the number on its own. It is where the line crosses the $y$-axis: when $x = 0$, $mx$ is 0, so $y = c$. Changing $c$ moves the whole line up or down. It does not change the steepness, because $m$ stays the same: $y = 2x + 4$ is $y = 2x + 1$ moved up 3. Lines with the same $m$ are **parallel**: equally steep, so they never meet. ```

# Graph boards for "What c does to a line". The rule is y = 2x + c unless a task needs m too; the dashed line
# y = 2x + 1 is where the line started, to compare with.

# region: run
widget: graph
x: -1, 5
y: -4, 14
slider c: -3, 6, 1
plot: y = 2x + c
plot: y = 2x + 1, dashed
table: 0, 1, 2, 3
step: 1
# endregion

# region: below
widget: graph
x: -1, 5
y: -6, 12
slider c: -5, 5, 1
plot: y = 2x + c
point T: 0, -2
# endregion

# region: origin
widget: graph
x: -1, 5
y: -6, 12
slider c: -5, 5, 2
plot: y = 2x + c
point T: 2, 4
# endregion

# region: off-axis
widget: graph
x: -1, 5
y: -6, 14
slider c: -5, 8, 0
plot: y = 2x + c
point T: 1, 6
# endregion

# region: parallel
widget: graph
x: -1, 5
y: -8, 8
slider m: -3, 3, 1
slider c: -5, 5, 2
plot: y = mx + c
plot: y = -x + 3, dashed
point T: 0, -1
# endregion

# region: make
widget: graph
x: -1, 5
y: -4, 12
slider c: -10, 12, 1
plot: y = 2x + c
plot: y = 2x + 1, dashed
point P: 3, -2, drag
# endregion

# region: explain
widget: graph
x: -1, 4
y: -6, 12
slider c: -2, 4, 1, 3
plot: y = 2x + c
plot: y = 2x + 1, dashed
# endregion

# region: explain-pic
widget: graph
x: -1, 4
y: -2, 14
plot: y = 2x + 4
plot: y = 2x + 1, dashed
point A: 0, 4
point B: 0, 1
# endregion
